blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
The deepest lesson of IT leadership is that, at the top, there is no separation between IT and the business. The systems are the business. The data is the business. The networks, the tools and the policies are how the company actually works every single day. A leader who treats IT as a separate world — something that happens over there, managed by specialists and reviewed quarterly — is describing a company that no longer exists.

The leaders who understand this stop asking how much IT costs and start asking how much it makes possible. They join strategy conversations with the CIO sitting beside them. They protect investments in infrastructure, security and data with the same seriousness they protect investments in people and brand. They speak honestly about trade-offs and accept, without drama, that some of the most important things their company does are invisible to everyone except the few engineers who keep them running.

Over a career, this quiet respect for IT as the shape of the business is what separates leaders who keep their companies relevant from those who quietly fall behind. At the end of every other track, technology was waiting underneath. At the end of this one, we arrive back where every serious senior leader eventually stands: treating the systems, the people who build them, and the decisions they enable as the same living thing. That is IT leadership. And that, honestly, is business leadership too.

items.q: According to the text, what mistake does a leader make by treating IT as "a separate world"?
options: They describe a company that no longer exists
items.why: "is describing a company that no longer exists" — separar TI do negócio é retratar uma empresa que já não existe.

items.q: How do the leaders who "understand this" reframe the question about IT?
options: From how fast it runs to how secure it is
From who manages it to who audits it
From how much it costs to how much it makes possible
From what it replaces to what it automates
items.why: "stop asking how much IT costs and start asking how much it makes possible".

items.q: The passage suggests that some of a company's most important work is…
options: the most expensive line on the budget
items.why: "invisible to everyone except the few engineers who keep them running".

items.q: Which statement would the author most likely DISAGREE with?
options: At the top, IT and the business are one and the same.
IT is a support function best reviewed quarterly and left to specialists.
The CIO belongs in strategy conversations.
Investments in data deserve the same seriousness as investments in brand.
items.why: Inferência: o texto inteiro argumenta contra tratar TI como função separada e periférica.

items.q: What does the closing line — "that, honestly, is business leadership too" — imply?
options: Business leaders should learn to code
IT leadership is a lesser form of leadership
The distinction between IT and business leadership dissolves at the top
Only engineers can lead a modern company
items.why: Inferência: o fecho retórico funde as duas ideias — liderar TI, no topo, é liderar o negócio.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Sophie encerrando a trilha de TI e o programa inteiro. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
So this is where we close — not just the IT track, but the whole Czarnikow programme. And I want to end where a senior leader eventually stands, rather than where most of us start.

When I began, I thought of technology as a service I requested. Someone kept the systems running, and I signed off on the budget once a year. What changed me was watching a single outage. For six hours we couldn't price, couldn't settle, couldn't move. And I understood, quite physically, that the systems were not supporting the business. They were the business.

So my ask to you is small but stubborn. Bring your CIO into the strategy room and keep them there. When you weigh a trade-off, name the data cost out loud, the way you'd name the people cost. And when an engineer keeps something invisible running for years, notice it — because nobody else will.

That quiet respect is the whole lesson. It won't appear on a slide, and it rarely shows up in a quarterly review. But over a career, it is what separates the leaders who stay relevant from the ones who quietly fall behind. Thank you — all of you — for the work.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What is Sophie closing in this talk?
options: The IT track and the whole Czarnikow programme
The strategy off-site for the year
items.why: "this is where we close — not just the IT track, but the whole Czarnikow programme."

items.q: What experience changed how Sophie saw technology?
items.why: "What changed me was watching a single outage… for six hours we couldn't price, couldn't settle, couldn't move."

items.q: What does Sophie ask her audience to do with the CIO?
options: Bring them into the strategy room and keep them there
Give them a larger annual budget
items.why: "Bring your CIO into the strategy room and keep them there."

items.q: When Sophie says the systems "were the business," she most likely means that…
options: the business cannot function apart from its systems
IT should report to the CEO directly
items.why: Inferência: sem os sistemas não se precifica, liquida ou opera — logo os sistemas são o próprio negócio.

items.q: Why does Sophie call her request "small but stubborn"?
options: It costs very little but is easy to ignore
It applies only to the IT department
It requires new software but little training
It is a modest habit that must be defended persistently
items.why: Inferência: é um gesto discreto (respeito silencioso) que não aparece em slides, então precisa ser mantido com teimosia.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "At the top, there is no separation between IT and the business." A separation is…
options: a division or distance between things
items.why: Separation = separação: uma divisão ou distância entre as coisas.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "They stopped asking what the platform costs and asked instead what it ___."
items.why: "to make possible" = tornar possível — a virada de foco defendida na lição.

items.q: Choose the correct term: "Every serious ___ that keeps the pricing engine running is invisible to the board."
items.why: Engineer = engenheiro: quem mantém os sistemas rodando nos bastidores.

items.q: Trade-off is best described as…
options: a balance in which gaining one thing means giving up another
items.why: Trade-off = compromisso: você ganha de um lado abrindo mão de outro.

items.q: "We treat the systems and the people as the same living thing." Here it means…
options: a biological organism in the office
an interconnected whole that grows and changes together
items.why: "Living thing" (coisa viva) é usada como metáfora: um todo integrado que evolui junto.

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem quando a liderança fala de TI e do negócio. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The board still has to sign off on the security investment." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "We'll roll out the new data platform desk by desk." To roll out means to…
items.why: Roll out = implementar de forma progressiva.

items.q: "Two directors pushed back on cutting the infrastructure budget." They…
items.why: Push back on = resistir, discordar — sem necessariamente rejeitar de vez.

items.q: "Naming the data cost won't move the needle unless leaders act on it." This means it will…
items.why: Move the needle = mexer o ponteiro, fazer diferença perceptível.

items.q: "The team agreed to protect the legacy system but never followed through." They…
options: failed to carry it to completion
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim o que foi combinado.
